import re

# Extract unemployment insurance tax data for 50 states (excluding DC, territories)

    'Tennessee': 169376,
    'Texas': 536530,
    'Utah': 60537,
    'Vermont': 8471,
    'Virginia': 162666,
    'Washington': 209293,
    'West Virginia': 13475,
    'Wisconsin': 117667,
    'Wyoming': 7638,
}

# Verify we have 50 states
print(f"Number of states: {len(data)}")

# Sort by value (descending) and assign rank
sorted_values = sorted(data.values(), reverse=True)
ranks = list(range(1, len(sorted_values) + 1))

# Calculate Zipf exponent using linear regression on log-log scale
# Zipf's law: value ∝ rank^(-s), so log(value) = -s * log(rank) + constant
# We fit: log(value) = a - s*log(rank), so s is the negative slope

import math
import statistics

log_ranks = [math.log10(r) for r in ranks]
log_values = [math.log10(v) for v in sorted_values]

# Linear regression
n = len(ranks)
mean_log_r = statistics.mean(log_ranks)
mean_log_v = statistics.mean(log_values)

# Calculate slope (s) using least squares
numerator = sum((log_ranks[i] - mean_log_r) * (log_values[i] - mean_log_v) for i in range(n))
denominator = sum((log_ranks[i] - mean_log_r) ** 2 for i in range(n))

slope = numerator / denominator

# Zipf exponent is the negative of the slope
zipf_exponent = -slope

print(f"Slope: {slope}")
print(f"Zipf exponent: {zipf_exponent}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(zipf_exponent, 3)}")

# Show top 10 for verification
print("\nTop 10 states by UI tax receipts:")
for i, (state, value) in enumerate(sorted(data.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:10]):
    print(f"  {i+1}. {state}: {value}")
